what_its_for: Vardenafil is used to treat erectile dysfunction (ED) in men. It helps you get and keep an erection firm enough for sexual activity by increasing blood flow to the penis when you are sexually stimulated.
how_to_take: Take vardenafil by mouth with or without food, about 1 hour before sexual activity. Swallow the regular tablet whole with a full glass of water. If you use the dissolving tablet (Staxyn), place it on your tongue and let it dissolve — do not chew it or swallow it whole, and do not take it with water. Only take it when you plan to have sexual activity — you still need to be sexually aroused for it to work.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg taken about 60 minutes before sexual activity. Your doctor may increase your dose to 20 mg or lower it to 5 mg depending on how well it works for you and any side effects you notice. Do not take more than one dose per day. Do not take more than 20 mg in a 24-hour period.
missed_dose: Vardenafil is taken only when needed, not on a regular daily schedule. Since it is not taken at set times, there is no missed dose to worry about. Never take two doses at the same time or take extra to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store vardenafil at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine properly.
what_to_avoid: Do not take vardenafil if you use nitrate medicines (such as nitroglycerin, isosorbide) for chest pain or heart problems — combining these can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice, as it can increase vardenafil levels in your blood. Limit alcohol, as it can lower blood pressure and make side effects worse. Avoid taking other ED medicines at the same time. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or lightheaded after taking vardenafil.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: an erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism) — this is a medical emergency that can cause permanent damage; sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes; sudden decrease or loss of hearing, ringing in your ears, or dizziness; chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or shortness of breath during or after sex; severe dizziness or fainting; or an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Vardenafil usually starts working within 30 to 60 minutes after taking it. Its effects can last for about 4 to 5 hours. Keep in mind that sexual stimulation is still required for the medicine to work — it will not cause an erection on its own.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Your doctor may start you on a lower dose of 5 mg because the medicine stays in your body longer as you age. Liver problems: If you have moderate liver disease, your doctor may lower your dose. Do not use if you have severe liver disease. Kidney problems: Dose adjustment may be needed for severe kidney disease. Women and children: Vardenafil is not approved for use in women or anyone under 18 years old. Always tell your doctor about all your health conditions and all medicines you take before starting vardenafil.
